biography: Ian "Stints" Stinton, a name synonymous with aggressive Ginetta racing, hails from the small town of Oundle, Northamptonshire. His journey began not on asphalt, but on the muddy fields of his family's farm, tearing around on a beat-up quad bike. This reckless abandon translated seamlessly to four wheels when, at 16, he entered a local karting championship, stunning seasoned veterans with his raw speed and fearless overtaking maneuvers. His defining moment came in the 2018 Ginetta GT4 SuperCup, where, despite starting from the back of the grid after a qualifying mishap, he carved his way through the field, clinching a dramatic last-lap victory. Now 33, Stinton is considered to be in his prime, consistently battling at the front of the pack, though often attracting the ire of his competitors with his uncompromising style. He continues to develop in the Ginetta series, pushing for a championship title that has narrowly evaded him in past seasons. His dedication and commitment to the Ginetta brand has made him a fan favorite.
drivingStyle: Stinton's driving style can be best described as 'controlled chaos'. He's known for late-braking maneuvers that often push the limits of adhesion, diving into corners with a ferocity that leaves little room for error. While some criticize his aggressive approach, few can deny its effectiveness when he's on form. He is constantly pushing his car to the very edge, using all available track width and often flirting with track limits. He manages tire wear with a calculated risk, often pushing hard early in a stint to gain track position, banking on his ability to hold off the competition later on.

careerHighlight: Winning the 2018 Ginetta GT4 SuperCup race at Brands Hatch after starting from the back of the grid, showcasing his exceptional overtaking skills.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the 2022 Ginetta GT4 SuperCup championship decider at Donington Park, losing the title by a single point.
